name: Meridian Coffee Roasters

do: Talk about the farmers and the roast, not just the flavour notes
Name origins, batch sizes and roast timing plainly, the way a log entry would
Say what a bag or box does not include as readily as what it does
Use everyday kitchen words for taste — sweet, nutty, sharp, bitter
dont: Never call the coffee artisanal, curated, craft or bespoke
Never call anything revolutionary, game-changing or the best in the world
Never describe flavour in abstract poetry such as notes of dusk or liquid velvet
Never call the reader a connoisseur, aficionado or coffee snob
Never imply the coffee is rare, exclusive or limited to a chosen few
Never pad a sentence with words like simply, truly, elevated or journey

offerings.name: Roaster's Choice Subscription
offerings.description: A rotating 340g bag of our current favourite single-origin, roasted fresh and delivered every four weeks.

offerings.name: Origins Gift Box
offerings.description: A one-time gift box with three 200g bags from three different origins, plus a tasting card.

positioning: For people who check the roast date before the price, Meridian roasts single-origin coffee in small batches only once an order exists and ships it within 48 hours — the exact opposite of a supermarket bag that has been on a shelf since before anyone thought about it.

composition_plan.intent: Name the roastery and the roast-to-order promise in the left rows and set one action beside a single flat field; no atmosphere, no wash, the index starts on the same screen.
Put the given figures on roasting cadence, batch size and shipping window under short plain labels, so the central claim is read as a record rather than a boast.
Run the sourcing and roast detail as a top-to-bottom index of full-width labelled rows, one idea per row, no cards — this is the run the archetype is built around.
Interrupt the run of rows with the single unlabelled wide statement about growers and honest buying, one narrow column of supporting detail beside it.
Lay the catalogue out side by side, one column per offering, so the two ways to buy are compared on the same lines rather than sold separately.
Show the sequence from order placed to bag arriving as an ordered list, one line each, making the timing promise legible as steps; numbering comes from the list itself.
Answer the practical questions and state the exclusions plainly, keeping the page honest about limits before anyone has to ask.
Close with the street address, email and phone so the neighbourhood roastery reads as a real place, and nothing else.
